headings: Implications of Being an Emerging Growth Company
paragraphs: FrontView is an internally-managed net-lease real estate investment trust ("REIT") that is experienced in acquiring, owning and managing properties with frontage that are net leased to a diversified group of tenants. We have selected the name "FrontView" to reflect our unique "real estate first" investment strategy. This approach targets properties with frontage located in prominent retail areas that can attract multiple tenants and can have replaceable rents. Our target properties have direct frontage on high-traffic roads, ensuring high visibility to consumers with adaptable spaces that can typically work for various usages. We are a growing net-lease REIT and own a well-diversified portfolio of 303 properties with direct frontage across 37 U.S. states as of December 31, 2025. FrontView's tenants typically include service-oriented businesses, such as medical and dental providers, quick service restaurants, casual dining, other service providers, financial institutions, cellular stores, automotive stores, fitness operators, discount retail, convenience stores and gas stations, automotive dealers, car washes, home improvement stores, other necessity tenants, pharmacies, as well as professional services tenants.

We typically invest in net-leased properties located in larger populated markets, within active retail corridors, and in areas with direct visibility on high-traffic roads. We believe our tenants value the prominent location of our properties for their core business operations. In addition, our tenants are able to retain operational control of their strategically important locations through long-term net leases.

As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio comprised approximately 2.7 million rentable square feet of operational space and was highly diversified based on tenant, industry, and geography. As of December 31, 2025, our properties were located in 37 U.S. states, with no single state exceeding 14.9% of our ABR with 78.1% of our properties in the top 100 MSAs. Our portfolio's occupancy rate was 98.7% as of December 31, 2025. Our properties were leased to 321 tenants that represented 155 different brands, with no single tenant brand accounting for more than 3.51% of our ABR. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 34.8% of our tenants had an investment-grade credit rating. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 97.3% of our leases (based on ABR) had contractual rent escalations, including the option terms. As of December 31, 2025, the ABR weighted average remaining term of our leases was approximately 7.4 years, excluding renewal options. As of December 31, 2025, no more than 11.1% of our rental revenue was derived from leases that expire in any single year prior to 2030. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we had total rental revenues of $66.5 million, a net loss of $5.6 million and funds from operations ("FFO") of $26.1 million.

FrontView REIT, Inc. was formed on June 23, 2023 as a Maryland corporation and is the successor to the Predecessor, a private net lease company formed in 2016 that focused on outparcel acquisitions. FrontView Operating Partnership LP (the "OP"), is the entity through which the Company conducts its business and owns all of the Company's properties either directly or indirectly through subsidiaries. Upon the closing of the initial public offering ("IPO"), the Company is the sole managing member of the OP. The units not owned by the Company in the OP are referred to as OP Units or non-controlling interests.

On October 2, 2024, the Company, through a series of REIT Contribution Transactions and completion of the Internalization, created an umbrella partnership real estate investment trust ("UPREIT") structure with a publicly-traded REIT that is internally managed and owns all of its assets and conducts all of its business through the OP.

On October 3, 2024, the Company completed its IPO on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the symbol "FVR" and issued 13,200,000 shares of Common Stock at an initial public offering price of $19.00 per share (the "IPO Price"). As part of the IPO, the underwriters were granted an option, exercisable within 30 days from October 3, 2024, to purchase up to an additional 1,980,000 shares of Common Stock at the IPO Price, less underwriting discounts and commissions. On October 23, 2024, the underwriters partially exercised their option by purchasing an additional 1,090,846 shares of common stock. The Company received total net proceeds of $271.5 million, net of transaction costs and underwriting discounts of $24.1 million.

To achieve an appropriate risk-adjusted return, we seek to maintain a highly diversified portfolio of properties located in prominent areas with direct frontage on high-traffic roads that are visible to consumers. We aim to ensure diversity across geographic locations, tenants, and brands, and to enable cross-diversification within each category. We discuss below our portfolio diversification based on several different metrics and information provided as of December 31, 2025.

We typically seek tenants that operate service-oriented businesses, such as restaurants, automotive, medical and dental providers, financial institutions, cellular stores, general retail, fitness, car wash, gas and convenience, other service, necessity, and discount concepts typically leased to national and regional brands and franchisees. As of December 31, 2025, our properties were occupied by 321 tenants that operated 155 different brands, with no single tenant brand accounting for more than 3.51% of our ABR.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Properties
Properties involve significant risks of tenant defaults and tenant vacancies, which could materially and adversely affect us.
We have limited opportunities to increase rents under our long-term leases with tenants, which could impede our growth and materially and adversely affect us.
The weighted average remaining term of our leases is 7.4 years, excluding renewal options, which will require us to undertake more re-leasing efforts that could materially and adversely affect us.
We may not be able to achieve growth through acquisitions at a rate that is comparable to our historical results, which could materially and adversely affect us.
We have experienced net losses for the past four years and we may experience additional net losses in the future.
We may not achieve the total returns we expect from our future acquisitions, which could materially and adversely affect us.

We may not be able to obtain acquisition financing or obtain other capital from third-party sources on favorable terms, or at all, which could materially and adversely affect our growth prospects and our business.
We may not be able to effectively manage our growth and any failure to do so could materially and adversely affect us.
As we continue to acquire properties pursuant to our growth strategy, our portfolio may become less diversified which could materially and adversely affect us.
We face significant competition for tenants, which could materially and adversely affect us, including our occupancy, rental rates, and results of operations.
The departure of any of our key personnel with long-standing business relationships could materially and adversely affect us.
Tenant demand for properties may decline, which could materially and adversely affect us.
Our portfolio is concentrated in certain states and MSAs and any adverse developments and/or economic downturns in these geographic markets could materially and adversely affect us.

Our portfolio of properties is also concentrated in certain tenant brands and industries, and any adverse developments relating to one or more of these brands or industries could materially and adversely affect us.

Our portfolio of properties is concentrated among tenants with non-investment grade credit ratings, and any adverse developments affecting the credit of these tenants could materially and adversely affect us.
Our assessment that many of our tenants' businesses are e-commerce resistant may prove to be incorrect, which could materially and adversely affect us.
The decrease in demand for restaurant properties may materially and adversely affect us.

If one or more of our top 20 tenant brands, which together represented approximately 39.3% of our ABR as of December 31, 2025, suffers a downturn in their business, it could materially and adversely affect us.
We may be unable to renew leases, re-lease properties as leases expire, or lease vacant spaces on favorable terms or at all, which, in each case, could materially and adversely affect us.
Our business is subject to significant re-leasing risk, particularly for specialty properties that are suitable for only one use, which could materially and adversely affect us.
We could face issues related to condemnation, government taking, environmental contamination or damage and or destruction of our properties for a number of different reasons.
We may experience tenant defaults, particularly from tenants that do not have an investment grade credit rating, which could materially and adversely affect us.

Our underwriting and risk management procedures that we use to evaluate a tenant's credit risk may fail, or otherwise not accurately reflect the risk of our investment, which could materially and adversely affect us.
Any failure of one or more tenants to provide accurate or complete financial information could prevent us from identifying tenant problems that could materially and adversely affect us.

If one or more of our tenants declares bankruptcy or becomes insolvent, then we may encounter significant difficulties in navigating those bankruptcy proceedings, which could materially and adversely affect us.
Some of our leases may require us to pay or reimburse tenants for property-related expenses, which could materially and adversely affect us.
Our business may be adversely affected by changes in U.S. trade policy, including the imposition of tariffs and resulting effects.

Security breaches and other technology disruptions could disrupt our operations, compromise our confidential information or information systems and expose us to liability, which could materially and adversely affect us.
The use of artificial intelligence presents risks and challenges that may adversely impact our business and operating results or that of our tenants.
Our properties may be subject to impairment charges which could materially and adversely affect us, including our financial condition.
We face risks associated with repositioning or construction of real estate projects, which may materially and adversely affect us.
Changes in accounting and reporting standards may materially and adversely affect us.
Certain provisions of our leases or loan agreements may be unenforceable, which could materially and adversely affect us.
We may become subject to litigation, which could materially and adversely affect us.
The costs of environmental contamination or liabilities related to environmental laws may materially and adversely affect us.
paragraphs: The following are some of the risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those presented in our forward-looking statements. You should consider carefully the risks described below and the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face but do represent those risks and uncertainties that we believe are material to us. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also harm our business.
• Properties involve significant risks of tenant defaults and tenant vacancies, which could materially and adversely affect us.
• We have limited opportunities to increase rents under our long-term leases with tenants, which could impede our growth and materially and adversely affect us.

• Our financial results have and may continue to fluctuate in the future, which makes predicting our revenues, costs and expenses difficult, and any volatility in our future financial results could materially and adversely affect us.
• We may not be able to achieve growth through acquisitions at a rate that is comparable to our historical results, which could materially and adversely affect us.
• We may not be able to effectively manage our growth and any failure to do so could materially and adversely affect us.

paragraphs: Except where the context suggests otherwise, as used in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the terms "FVR," "we," "us," "our," and "our company" refer to FrontView REIT, Inc., a Maryland corporation incorporated on June 23, 2023, and, as required by context, FrontView Operating Partnership LP, a Delaware limited partnership, which we refer to as the or our "OP", and to their respective subsidiaries.

The following Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") is intended to help the reader understand our results of operations and financial condition. This MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements appearing in Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplemental Data" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We are an internally-managed net-lease REIT that is experienced in acquiring, owning and managing properties with frontage that are net leased to a diversified group of tenants. We are a growing net-lease REIT and owned a well-diversified portfolio of 303 properties across 37 U.S. states as of December 31, 2025. Our tenants include service-oriented businesses, such as medical and dental providers, quick service restaurants, casual dining, financial institutions, cellular stores, automotive stores, automotive services, convenience stores and gas stations, general retail, discount retail, automotive dealers, fitness operators, car washes, pharmacies, home improvement stores, as well as professional services tenants.

We currently derive a majority of our revenue from rents received from individual tenants of each of our properties in our portfolio. Our properties are typically leased under long-term net leases. As of December 31, 2025, we had ABR of $62.9 million with a weighted average remaining term of our leases was approximately 7.4 years, excluding renewal options. Approximately 97.3% of our leases (based on ABR) had contractual rent escalations, including, in some cases, pursuant to option terms. As of December 31, 2025, we had 321 tenants that represented 155 different brands. Our top 10 tenant brands (based on ABR) represented approximately 23.7% of our portfolio ABR as of December 31, 2025.

In connection with our initial public offering on October 2, 2024, we completed the Internalization pursuant to which we began directly employing employees and entered into employment agreements with each of our named executive officers. In addition, the Internalization eliminated the management and other fees and carried interest provisions that were previously paid by our Predecessor. The historical results of operations for our Predecessor through October 2, 2024, include the payment of management fees that we no longer pay following the Internalization and do not include the direct compensation expense, or other asset management, acquisition or general and administrative expenses not previously incurred based upon our externally managed structure.

As of December 31, 2025, we had total debt of $315.5 million, Net Debt of $302.0 million, a Net Debt to Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre ratio of 5.6x and a Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio of 3.6x. Net Debt, Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre and Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio are non-GAAP financial measures, and Annualized Adjusted EBITDAre is calculated based upon EBITDA, EBITDAre, and Adjusted EBITDAre, each of which is also a non-GAAP financial measure. Refer to Non-GAAP Measures below for further details concerning our calculation of non-GAAP measures and reconciliations to the comparable GAAP measure.

Our results of operations and financial condition are affected by numerous factors, many of which are beyond our control. Key factors that impact our results of operations and financial condition include rental rates, lease renewals and occupancy, land values, acquisition volume, tenant growth, demand, expansion, construction costs, net-lease terms, market liquidity, financing arrangements and leverage, property dispositions, general and administrative expenses, inflation, interest rates, consumer confidence, the overall economic environment and the financial strength of our tenants.

Our ability to grow rental revenue from our existing portfolio will depend on our ability to realize the rental escalations built into our leases and execute lease renewals and lease extensions. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 97.3% of our leases (based on ABR) had contractual rent escalations, including, in some cases, pursuant to options terms, with an ABR weighted average annual minimum increase of approximately 1.7%. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 96.3% of our leases (based on ABR) contained fixed annual rent increases or periodic escalations over the term of the lease (e.g. a 10% increase every five years), approximately 1.0% of our leases (based on ABR) contained annual lease escalations based on increases in the CPI, and the remaining approximately 2.7% of our leases (based on ABR) did not contain rent escalation provisions. During periods of inflation, our fixed rent increases may not keep pace with the rate of inflation while the limited number of our leases that include CPI-based increases may fare better. Conversely, during periods where inflation is more limited, our leases with fixed rate increases may fare better than our leases with CPI-based increases.

From time to time, we may seek to sell any of our properties, in particular, where we believe the risk profile may have changed and become misaligned with our then current portfolio acquisition objectives. We also may selectively decide to sell properties that no longer meet one or more of our investment criteria or that may be sold opportunistically. The resulting gains or losses on any future dispositions may materially impact our operating results. The recognition of a gain or loss on the sale of real estate varies from transaction to transaction based on fluctuations in asset prices and demand in the real estate market at the time a property is listed for sale. As of December 31, 2025, we have sold 47 properties since inception.

As of December 31, 2025, the weighted average remaining term of our leases was approximately 7.4 years, excluding renewal options. The stability of the rental revenue generated by our properties depends principally on our tenants' ability to pay rent and our ability to collect rent, our ability to renew expiring leases or re-lease space upon the expiration or other termination of leases, our ability to lease properties that become vacant and maintain or increase rental rates at our leased properties. To the extent our properties become vacant, including through casualty, condemnation, weather and environmental contamination, we would forego rental income while remaining responsible for the payment of property taxes, insurance, maintenance and other related costs and maintaining the property until it is re-leased, which could negatively impact our operating results. As of December 31, 2025, we had four vacant properties.

Our historical growth in revenues and earnings has been achieved through rent escalations associated with existing in-place leases, coupled with rental income generated from property acquisitions. Our ability to grow revenue will depend, to a significant degree, on our ability to acquire additional properties. Our ability to grow requires us to identify and complete acquisitions that meet our investment criteria. Changes in capitalization rates, interest rates, inflation, market competition, economic changes, property inventory, and other factors may impact our acquisition opportunities in the future. Market conditions may also impact the total returns we can achieve on our investments. Our acquisition volume also depends on our ability to successfully access third-party debt and equity financing to fund our capital needs. As of December 31, 2025, we have bought 350 properties since inception.

Substantially all of our leases are net leases pursuant to which our tenants generally are obligated to pay customary expenses associated with the leased property such as real estate taxes, insurance, maintenance and repairs, and in many cases capital costs. Some leases contain exceptions that require us to pay specified expenses such as the cost of roof, parking lot, heating, ventilation and air conditioning and structure and non-structural repairs and replacement costs, off-site improvements, lease covenants affecting off-site property, and remediation activities (unless necessitated by the tenant), as well as costs related to the operation of a property in excess of certain caps contained within the underlying lease. In certain instances, a landlord's reimbursement obligation may include reimbursing the tenant for the unamortized costs of certain expenses incurred by the tenant for the development of the premises. In some leases, this type of reimbursement obligation is triggered by the default of the landlord under the lease, but other leases require reimbursement of the tenant due to circumstances outside of the landlord's control. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we incurred approximately $1.8 million in aggregate of expenses that were not tenant obligations. To the extent that our properties experience an increase in roof and structure, capital or other repairs or costs for which we are contractually responsible under some leases, it could negatively impact our future operating results. In addition, an increase in the number of leases in which we are responsible for some or all of these expenses could negatively influence our future operating results.

As of December 31, 2025, our debt capital was comprised of a floating rate Term Loan and a floating rate Revolving Credit Facility. Accordingly, we are subject to interest rate risk. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we entered into interest rate swap agreements to manage interest rate exposure on both the Term Loan and Revolving Credit Facility. Refer to the discussion in the Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities section below for further details. We also expect to continue to incur debt in the future in order to fund future acquisitions, which we expect will increase the amount of interest expense we incur. In addition, although we plan to manage our total floating-rate debt exposure, changes in the interest rate environment could either increase or decrease our weighted average interest rate in the future or impact any refinancing initiatives, which could also result in principal reduction requirements and ultimate refinancing risks. Any changes to our debt structure, including borrowings under our Revolving Credit Facility and Term Loan, or debt financing associated with property acquisitions, could materially influence our operating results.

headings: 本公司不動產投資組合
{'original': 'Implications of Being an Emerging Growth Company', 'translated': '作為新興成長公司之影響'}
paragraphs: FrontView 是一家 internally-managed net-lease 不動產投資信託 ("REIT")，專門從事取得、擁有及管理具有正面街景的不動產，並以多元化租戶羣進行 net lease。我們選擇 "FrontView" 這個名稱，是為了反映我們獨特的 "不動產為先" 投資策略。此策略目標為位於知名零售地區、能吸引多個租戶且租金可更換的不動產。我們的目標不動產具有直接正面街景，位於高流量道路，確保對消費者有高可見度，且空間可調整，通常可適應多種用途。我們是一家成長中的 net-lease REIT，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，擁有 303 個具正面街景的不動產，分佈於美國 37 個州。FrontView 的租戶通常包括服務導向的企業，例如醫療與牙科服務提供者、速食餐廳、休閒餐廳、其他服務提供者、金融機構、行動電話商店、汽車商店、健身經營者、折扣零售、便利商店與加油站、汽車經銷商、洗車店、家用品商店、其他必需租戶、藥房，以及專業服務租戶。
我們通常投資於位於人口較多市場、活躍零售走廊，以及具直接正面街景於高流量道路的 net-leased 不動產。我們相信租戶重視我們不動產的顯著位置，以進行其核心業務運作。此外，租戶能透過長期 net lease 保留其戰略重要位置的運營控制權。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的資產組合包含約 2.7 百萬平方英呎的可出租空間，並根據租戶、產業與地理分佈高度分散。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的不動產位於美國 37 個州，無任何單一州超過我們 ABR 的 14.9%，其中 78.1% 的不動產位於前 100 大都會區。我們的資產組合的佔用率為 98.7%，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。我們的不動產出租給 321 個租戶，代表 155 個不同品牌，無任何單一租戶品牌佔我們 ABR 的 3.51% 以上。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約 34.8% 的租戶擁有投資等級信用評等。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約 97.3% 的租約（根據 ABR）包含契約租金調漲，包括選擇權條款。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們租約的 ABR 加權平均剩餘年限為約 7.4 年，不包含續約選擇權。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，無任何單一租約在 2030 年前到期的租金收入超過 11.1%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的總租金收入為 66.5 百萬美元，淨虧損為 5.6 百萬美元，以及資金從運作 ("FFO") 為 26.1 百萬美元。

FrontView REIT, Inc. 於 2023 年 6 月 23 日成立為馬裏蘭州公司，並為 Predecessor 的繼承者，Predecessor 是一家於 2016 年成立的私人 net lease 公司，專注於 outparcel 收購。FrontView Operating Partnership LP（"OP"）是本公司進行業務與擁有所有不動產的實體，無論是直接或透過子公司。在初始公開發行（"IPO"）完成後，本公司為 OP 的唯一管理成員。OP 中未由本公司持有的單位稱為 OP 單位或非控制性權益。
於 2024 年 10 月 2 日，本公司透過一系列 REIT 貢獻交易及內部化完成，與一家公開上市的 REIT 創建了一個傘型合夥實體不動產投資信託（"UPREIT"）結構，該 REIT 為 internally-managed 並擁有其所有資產，並透過 OP 進行所有業務。

於 2024 年 10 月 3 日，本公司在紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）完成 IPO，股票代碼為 "FVR"，發行 13,200,000 股普通股，發行價格為每股 19.00 美元（"IPO Price"）。作為 IPO 的一部分，經紀人獲得了在 2024 年 10 月 3 日起 30 日內可購買最多 1,980,000 股普通股的選擇權，價格為 IPO Price，扣除經紀折扣與佣金。於 2024 年 10 月 23 日，經紀人部分行使選擇權，購買了額外 1,090,846 股普通股。本公司收到總淨資金為 271.5 百萬美元，扣除交易成本與經紀折扣 24.1 百萬美元。
為達到適當的風險調整回報，我們致力於維持高度分散的不動產資產組合，位於顯著地區，具直接正面街景於高流量道路，對消費者可見。我們旨在確保在地理分佈、租戶與品牌之間的多樣性，並在每個類別內實現交叉分散。我們在下文中討論我們的資產組合分散情況，根據多種不同指標及截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的資訊。
我們通常尋求經營服務導向業務的租戶，例如餐廳、汽車、醫療與牙科服務提供者、金融機構、行動電話商店、一般零售、健身、洗車、加油站與便利商店、其他服務、必需與折扣概念，通常出租給全國與區域品牌及特許經營者。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的不動產由 321 個租戶經營，代表 155 個不同品牌，無任何單一租戶品牌佔我們 ABR 的 3.51% 以上。

paragraphs: 除非上下文另有說明，否則本年度報告表10-K中所使用的「FVR」、「我們」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的公司」，均指FrontView REIT, Inc.，一家於2023年6月23日於馬裏蘭州成立的公司，並依上下文需要，指FrontView Operating Partnership LP，一家德克薩斯州的有限責任合夥企業，我們稱之為「OP」，以及其各自之子公司。
以下為管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析（「MD&A」），旨在協助讀者瞭解我們的營運成果與財務狀況。此MD&A為補充資料，應與我們之合併財務報表及附屬之財務報表附註一併閱讀，請參見本年度報告表10-K中第8項「財務報表與補充資料」。

我們是一家內部管理的淨租賃REIT，經驗豐富於取得、擁有及管理具有前街面的不動產，並以多元化租戶羣進行淨租賃。我們是一家成長中的淨租賃REIT，截至2025年12月31日，我們擁有位於美國37個州的303處不動產。我們的租戶包括服務導向的企業，例如醫療與牙科服務提供者、速食餐廳、輕食餐廳、金融機構、行動電話商店、汽車商店、汽車服務、便利商店與加油站、一般零售、折扣零售、汽車經銷商、健身經營者、汽車洗車場、藥房、家庭改善商店，以及專業服務租戶。
在2024年10月2日我們的首次公開發行中，我們完成了內部化程序，開始直接僱用員工，並與我們的知名高階主管簽訂僱用契約。此外，內部化程序消除了先前由我們前身所支付的管理費與其他費用及收益權條款。我們前身截至2024年10月2日的歷史營運結果，包含支付管理費的項目，而我們在內部化後不再支付這些費用，且不包含直接薪資支出或其他資產管理、收購或一般及行政費用，這些費用在先前的外部管理結構中並未產生。

截至2025年12月31日，我們總債務為315.5 百萬美元，淨債務為302.0 百萬美元，淨債務對年化調整後EBITDAre比率為5.6倍，固定負擔覆蓋比率為3.6倍。淨債務、年化調整後EBITDAre及固定負擔覆蓋比率為非GAAP財務指標，年化調整後EBITDAre是根據EBITDA、EBITDAre及調整後EBITDAre計算，這些皆為非GAAP財務指標。請參見下方「非GAAP指標」以瞭解我們計算非GAAP指標及與對應GAAP指標的調整細節。
我們的營運成果與財務狀況受到許多因素影響，其中許多因素超出我們的控制範疇。影響我們營運成果與財務狀況的關鍵因素包括租金率、租賃續約與佔用率、地價、收購量、租戶成長、需求、擴張、建設成本、淨租賃條款、市場流動性、融資安排與槓桿、不動產處分、一般及行政費用、通貨膨脹、利率、消費者信心、總體經濟環境以及租戶的財務強度。

我們從現有投資組閤中增加租金收入的能力，將取決於我們能否實現租賃中內建的租金調漲，並成功執行租賃續約與租賃延長。截至2025年12月31日，約97.3%的租賃（基於ABR）包含合約租金調漲，包括某些情況下依選項條款，其ABR加權平均年度最低調漲幅度約為1.7%。截至2025年12月31日，約96.3%的租賃（基於ABR）包含固定年度租金調漲或租賃期間內的定期調漲（例如每五年增加10%），約1.0%的租賃（基於ABR）包含根據CPI增加而調整的年度租金調漲，剩餘約2.7%的租賃（基於ABR）不包含租金調漲條款。在通貨膨脹期間，我們的固定租金調漲可能無法跟上通貨膨脹率，而我們有限的包含CPI調整的租賃可能表現較佳。相反地，在通貨膨脹較有限的時期，我們的固定租金調漲租賃可能表現優於包含CPI調整的租賃。

不時，我們可能尋求出售我們的任何不動產，特別是在我們認為風險特性已改變且與我們當時的投資目標不一致的情況下。我們也可能選擇性地決定出售不再符合我們一個或多個投資標準的不動產，或在適當的時機出售。任何未來處置所產生的損益，可能對我們的營運結果產生重大影響。出售不動產所認列的損益，因交易而異，取決於資產價格波動及不動產市場在該不動產上市銷售時的需求情況。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們自成立以來已出售 47 間不動產。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們租賃的平均剩餘租期約為 7.4 年，不包括續約選項。我們不動產產生的租金收入穩定性，主要取決於租戶支付租金的能力與我們收取租金的能力、我們續約到期租約或在租約到期或其他終止租約後重新出租空間的能力，以及我們出租空置不動產並維持或提高出租不動產租金的能力。若我們的不動產變為空置，包括因意外、徵收、天氣及環境污染所致，我們將放棄租金收入，同時仍需承擔地稅、保險、維護及其他相關費用，並維持該不動產直至重新出租，這可能對我們的營運結果產生負面影響。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們有四處空置不動產。

我們歷來營收與獲利的成長，是透過現有在場租約的租金調漲，以及透過不動產購入所產生的租金收入。我們成長營收的能力，將在很大程度上取決於我們取得更多不動產的能力。我們成長的潛力，需要我們識別並完成符合我們投資標準的購入。資本化率、利率、通貨膨脹、市場競爭、經濟變動、不動產存貨及其他因素，可能影響我們未來的購入機會。市場條件也可能影響我們在投資上所能達到的總回報。我們的購入數量也取決於我們成功取得第三方債務與權益融資以資助我們資本需求的能力。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們自成立以來已購入 350 間不動產。

我們的租賃幾乎全部為淨租賃，根據租賃條款，租戶通常負擔與租賃不動產相關的慣常費用，例如地稅、保險、維護與修繕費用，以及許多情況下的資本費用。某些租賃條款包含例外條款，要求我們支付特定費用，例如屋頂、停車場、供暖、通風與空調、結構與非結構性修繕與更換費用、離場改善、影響離場不動產的租賃契約條款，以及整治活動（除非因租戶所致），以及與租賃條款中所含的費用上限相比，與不動產運作相關的費用。在某些情況下，地主的補償義務可能包括補償租戶因開發租賃場地而產生的未償還費用。在一些租賃條款中，這種補償義務是由地主在租賃中違約所觸發，但其他租賃條款則因地主無法控制的情況而要求補償租戶。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們因非租戶義務而產生的費用總計約為 1.8 百萬美元。若我們的不動產因屋頂與結構、資本或其他修繕或費用增加，而根據某些租賃條款我們負有合同責任，這可能對我們未來的營運結果產生負面影響。此外，我們負有合同責任的租賃條款數量增加，也可能對我們未來的營運結果產生負面影響。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的債務資本由浮動利率的過渡貸款及浮動利率的週轉信用融資組成。因此，我們面臨利率風險。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度內，我們簽訂了利率交換協議，以管理過渡貸款及週轉信用融資的利率風險。請參閱下方「衍生金融工具及避險活動」部分的討論，以取得更多細節。我們也預期未來會繼續發行債務以資助未來的購入，這預期會增加我們的利息費用。此外，雖然我們計畫管理總浮動利率債務的風險，但利率環境的變化可能增加或減少我們未來的加權平均利率，或影響任何重組計畫，這也可能導致本金減少需求及最終重組風險。我們的債務結構任何變動，包括過渡貸款及週轉信用融資下的借款，或與不動產購入相關的債務融資，都可能對我們的營運結果產生重大影響。

headings: 與本公司業務及不動產相關之風險

我們在與租戶簽訂之長期租賃契約下，有限制提高租金之機會，這可能阻礙我們之成長，並對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
我們之租賃契約平均剩餘年限為 7.4 年，不計續約選項，這將需要我們進行更多重新出租之努力，可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
我們可能無法以與歷史結果相當之速度透過收購實現成長，這可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
我們已連續四年出現淨虧損，未來可能繼續出現淨虧損。
我們可能無法實現未來收購所預期之總回報，這可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
本公司可能無法以有利條件或任何方式取得收購融資或其他來自第三方的資金，這可能會對本公司成長潛力及業務造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司可能無法有效管理成長，若未能做到，可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
隨著本公司根據成長策略持續取得不動產，本公司資產組合可能會變得較不分散，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司面臨租戶競爭的壓力，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響，包括出租率、租金水平及營運成果。
本公司任何關鍵人員離職，尤其是與本公司有長期商業關係的員工，可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
租戶對不動產的需求可能下降，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司資產組合集中於某些州及都會區，若這些地理市場出現不利發展及/或經濟衰退，可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司資產組合亦集中於某些租戶品牌及產業，若這些品牌或產業出現不利發展，可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司不動產投資組合主要集中於信用評等非投資等級之租戶，若這些租戶信用狀況出現不利發展，將可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
本公司認為許多租戶之業務為抗風險於電商模式，此評估可能錯誤，將可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
餐飲不動產需求下降，可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
若本公司前20大租戶品牌中之一或數個，其業務表現出現下滑，而這些品牌於2025年12月31日時合計約佔本公司可變現租金（ABR）之39.3%，將可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
本公司可能無法續約租賃、於租約到期後重新出租不動產，或以有利條件出租空置空間，於每種情況下，均可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
本公司業務面臨顯著的重新出租風險，特別是針對僅適合單一用途之專業不動產，將可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
本公司可能面臨因徵收、政府強製取得、環境污染或損害及不動產遭毀壞等問題，而這些問題可能因多種原因發生。
本公司可能遭遇租戶違約，特別是來自信用評等非投資等級之租戶，將可能對本公司造成重大且不利影響。
本公司用以評估租戶信用風險的承保及風險管理程序，可能失敗，或無法準確反映投資風險，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
若一個或一個以上租戶未能提供準確或完整的財務資訊，可能會導致本公司無法識別租戶問題，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
若一個或一個以上租戶宣告破產或成為無清償能力，本公司可能會在處理這些破產程序時遭遇重大困難，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司部分租約可能要求本公司支付或補償租戶與不動產相關的費用，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
美國貿易政策的變動，包括課徵關稅及其衍生影響，可能會對本公司業務造成不利影響。
安全事件及其它科技中斷可能幹擾本公司運作，危及本公司機密資訊或資訊系統，並使本公司面臨法律責任，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響。
人工智慧的應用可能帶來風險與挑戰，可能對本公司或租戶的業務與營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司不動產可能面臨減值提列，這可能會對本公司造成重大且不利的影響，包括財務狀況。
我們面臨因重新定位或興建不動產項目而產生的風險，該等風險可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
會計及報導準則的變更可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們租賃或貸款協議中的某些條款可能無法執行，該等情況可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們可能成為訴訟的當事人，該等情況可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
環境污染的清理成本或與環境法規相關的責任可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
paragraphs: 下列為可能導致我們實際結果與我們在前瞻性陳述中所呈現結果有重大差異的風險與不確定性。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關附註。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險，但這些風險與不確定性為我們認為對我們而言屬重大者。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或目前認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務造成損害。
• 不動產涉及租戶違約及租戶空置的顯著風險，這可能會對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
• 我們在長期租賃契約中與租戶所訂的租金上調機會有限，這可能會阻礙我們的成長，並對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
• 我們的財務結果已並可能持續在未來出現波動，這使得預測我們的收入、成本及費用變得困難，且我們未來財務結果的任何波動都可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
• 我們可能無法以與歷史結果相當的速度透過收購來實現成長，這可能會對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
• 我們可能無法有效地管理我們的成長，且任何未能做到的狀況都可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
